_comment:
Fallout 3 record layouts. This directory is an overlay on schemas/fnv: it defines only the records whose layout differs, and everything else is read from FNV's. A record defined here is defined in full, because Schema::merge_str replaces a record rather than merging its subrecords, so a partial definition would silently drop the subrecords FNV knows.

Measured with NVRE's own coverage binary against all six shipped Fallout 3 masters (2026-10-20):

  Fallout3.esm    2,634,084 subrecords  ok 2,634,080 (100.00%)  unknown 3  trailing 0  error 1
  Anchorage.esm     177,986              ok   177,986 (100.00%)  unknown 0  trailing 0  error 0
  ThePitt.esm       136,807              ok   136,807 (100.00%)  unknown 0  trailing 0  error 0
  BrokenSteel.esm   174,525              ok   174,525 (100.00%)  unknown 0  trailing 0  error 0
  PointLookout.esm  235,206              ok   235,201 (100.00%)  unknown 5  trailing 0  error 0
  Zeta.esm          125,879              ok   125,879 (100.00%)  unknown 0  trailing 0  error 0

Those numbers are FNV's schema reading FO3's files, which is why the overlay is four records and not 107: the container, the group tree, the FormID model and almost every layout are shared between the two engines. What differs is listed below, each with the measurement behind it.

CONT.name: Container
CONT.note: Fallout 3 CONT: FNV's four subrecords plus MODS. Fallout 3's container carries the same alternate-texture list the other wbTexturedModel types do [documented: xEdit; observed: 5 instances in PointLookout.esm].

MODS.name: Biped Model Alternate Textures
MODS.note: xEdit declares the MODS family under wbTexturedModel (ARMO, STAT, ACTI, DOOR, WEAP, ALCH, TERM, HDPT, ARMA) and CONT carries the same model collection. schemas/fnv defines MODS on nine types but not on CONT, so FO3's five instances in PointLookout.esm read as unknown. Layout verified against those five: u32 count, then per entry a len_string model name, a formid and an i32 index. e.g. 01 00 00 00 | 0f 00 00 00 | "BurialMound03:0" | d6 28 00 01 | 00 00 00 00.

DOBJ.name: Default Object Manager
DOBJ.note: Fallout 3 DOBJ: 21 default objects where New Vegas has 34. The subrecord's own length is the field count, so a save writes 84 bytes rather than growing the record to New Vegas's 136.

DATA.name: Default Objects
DATA.note: Fallout 3's DOBJ DATA is 21 formids = 84 bytes, where New Vegas's is 34 = 136. fopdoc Fallout3/DOBJ lists 23 fields, which would be 92 bytes; the shipped record is 84, so the record wins over the spec — the game writes 21 of the 23 it documents, and the two it omits are not distinguishable from the bytes alone. Observed: the single instance in Fallout3.esm (00000031, 84 bytes) resolves field-for-field against fopdoc's order, every value a plausible FormID or a legitimate 0. The 13 New Vegas fields it lacks are Miss Fortune, the meltdown explosion, the five unarmed pickup-animations, the spotter/item-detected/cateye effects — all New Vegas additions.

PACK.name: Package
PACK.note: Fallout 3 PACK: FNV's subrecords plus IDLB. Fallout 3 has no PKPT/PKW3/PUID/PKAM/PKDD/PLD2 — those are New Vegas additions — and an unused subrecord on a record is simply absent rather than an error, so FNV's superset reads FO3's packages cleanly.

IDLB.name: Unused
IDLB.note: fopdoc Fallout3/PACK and FalloutNV/PACK both list IDLB 'Unused' byte[4] after IDLA, but schemas/fnv omits it. Observed: 1 instance in Fallout3.esm (000207E5), 4 bytes, value 1 — the field is named Unused and the game wrote 1 in it, so the bytes are copied through rather than assumed zero. Both games' packages carry it; adding it here fixes FNV's coverage too, but FNV's own masters happen not to use it.

IDLC.name: Idle Count
IDLC.note: xEdit wbIdleAnimation; 3 unused bytes only below form version 14

INAM.name: Idle
INAM.note: xEdit PACK OnBegin/OnEnd/OnChange INAM (IDLE or null)

PKDT.name: General
PKDT.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas PACK PKDT, SetOptionalFrom(2); flag names from wbDefinitionsCommon.pas wbPackageFlags (the FO3 names apply to FNV, wbIsFallout3 covers both games). Bit 20 is 'Head-Tracking Off' there and in the GECK wiki's flag list, 'Armor Unequipped' in JIP's GetPackageFlag list. The type-specific flags are a union decided by the package type (wbPKDTSpecificFlagsDecider): Find/Escort/Eat bits 8-10 Allow Buying/Killing/Stealing; Wander/Sandbox bits 0-5 No Eating/Sleeping/Conversation/Idle Markers/Furniture/Wandering; Use Item At bit 2 Sit Down plus 8-10; Ambush bit 0 Hide While Ambushing; Guard bit 3 Remain Near Reference to Guard. Kept as u16 here; fnv-ai reads it by type.

PLD2.name: Location 2
PLD2.note: xEdit PACK PLD2 (it appears twice in xEdit's list, the second as 'Location 2 (again??)'), same layout as PLDT

PLDT.name: Location 1
PLDT.note: xEdit PACK PLDT; the location field is a union decided by the type (wbPxDTLocationDecider): 0 reference FormID, 1 cell FormID, 4 base object FormID, 5 object type (wbObjectTypeEnum), otherwise unused. Kept as u32; fnv-ai maps FormIDs by type.

POBA.name: OnBegin Marker
POBA.note: xEdit PACK OnBegin group: POBA, then INAM idle, an embedded script, TNAM topic

POCA.name: OnChange Marker
POCA.note: xEdit PACK OnChange group, as OnBegin

POEA.name: OnEnd Marker
POEA.note: xEdit PACK OnEnd group, as OnBegin

PSDT.name: Schedule
PSDT.note: xEdit PACK PSDT: month -1 Any, 0-11 January-December, 12-15 Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter (records of form version below 122 store it zero-based; FNV records are version 15); date 0 Any, else day of month; time -1 Any, else 0-23 hour

PTD2.name: Target 2
PTD2.note: xEdit PACK PTD2, same layout as PTDT

PTDT.name: Target 1
PTDT.note: xEdit PACK PTDT, SetOptionalFrom(3); the target field is a union decided by the type: 0 reference FormID, 1 base object FormID, 2 object type (wbObjectTypeEnum), 3 unused (linked reference)

TNAM.name: Topic
TNAM.note: xEdit PACK OnBegin/OnEnd/OnChange TNAM (DIAL or null)

REGN.name: Region
REGN.note: Fallout 3 REGN: FNV's subrecords plus ICON, MICO, RDGS and RDMD, all four Fallout-3-only per fopdoc Fallout3/REGN.

ICON.name: Large Icon
ICON.note: fopdoc Fallout3/REGN: ICON 'Large icon filename' cstring. Fallout 3's region carries an icon; New Vegas's does not declare one. Not observed in the six shipped masters, so the layout is fopdoc's, not measured.

MICO.name: Small Icon
MICO.note: fopdoc Fallout3/REGN: MICO 'Small icon filename' cstring. As ICON: documented, not observed in the shipped masters.

RDAT.name: Data Header
RDAT.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN wbRegionDataEntries: type (2 objects, 3 weather, 4 map, 5 land, 6 grass, 7 sound, 8 imposter), flags, priority; repeated, each followed by that type's data

RDGS.name: Grasses
RDGS.note: fopdoc Fallout3/REGN Region Data Entry: RDGS 'Grasses', an array of grass formid plus 4 unknown bytes. Fallout 3 only: New Vegas's REGN has no RDGS. Documented, not observed in the shipped masters.

RDID.name: Imposters
RDID.note: The region's imposter list: the references with the REFR XSRF Imposter flag that are drawn always while the player is in the region [documented: GECK wiki 'Reference', owner's export]. Observed in FalloutNV.esm: present only after an RDAT of type 8, in 18 regions (StripImposter lists 222 references, StripImposterClose 10), each entry a REFR FormID; the subrecord name is not checked against xEdit

RDMD.name: Music Type
RDMD.note: fopdoc Fallout3/REGN Region Data Entry: RDMD 'Music Type' uint32 enum (0 Default, 1 Public, 2 Dungeon). Fallout 3 only; New Vegas's REGN defines RDMO/RDSI/RDSB for music but no RDMD. Observed: 2 instances in Fallout3.esm, both 4 bytes, both 0 (0001F959 and 00000A0B) — the enum's 'Default'. FNV's schema does not define RDMD at all, which is why those two read as unknown.

RDMO.name: Music
RDMO.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN sound data entry (RDMO, MUSC)

RDMP.name: Map Name
RDMP.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN Map entry: wbString(RDMP, 'Map Name', 0, cpTranslate).SetDontShow(wbREGNMapDontShow). Verified: 55 instances in FalloutNV.esm, all NUL-terminated (e.g. 'Aerotech Office Park\0', 'North Vegas Square\0')

RDOT.name: Objects
RDOT.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN Objects entry: wbArray(RDOT, 'Objects', wbStruct('Object', [wbFormIDCk('Object', [TREE, STAT, LTEX]), wbInteger('Parent Index', itU16, wbHideFFFF), wbUnused(2), wbFloat('Density'), wbInteger('Clustering', itU8), wbInteger('Min Slope', itU8), wbInteger('Max Slope', itU8), wbInteger('Flags', itU8, wbFlags([...])), wbInteger('Radius wrt Parent', itU16), wbInteger('Radius', itU16), wbFloat('Min Height'), wbFloat('Max Height'), wbFloat('Sink'), wbFloat('Sink Variance'), wbFloat('Size Variance'), wbStruct('Angle Variance', [itU16 X, Y, Z]), wbUnused(2), wbByteArray('Unknown', 4)])). Verified: every RDOT size in FalloutNV.esm is 52*n (52..520), plus one 0-byte and one 364 (7*52) case; no count prefix - the subrecord body is exactly N fixed-size elements (all sizes are multiples of 52)

RDSB.name: Battle MediaSet
RDSB.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN sound data entry (repeated RDSB 'Battle MediaSets', MSET)

RDSD.name: Sounds
RDSD.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsCommon.pas wbRegionSounds: wbArrayS(RDSD, 'Sounds', wbStructSK([0], 'Sound', [wbFormIDCk('Sound', [SNDR, SOUN, NULL]), wbInteger('Flags', itU32, wbFlags([Pleasant, Cloudy, Rainy, Snowy])), wbFloat('Chance')])). Verified: every RDSD size in FalloutNV.esm is a multiple of 12 (12..828), matching a u32 count plus 12-byte elements; no count prefix - the subrecord body is exactly N fixed-size elements (all sizes are multiples of 12)

RDSI.name: Incidental MediaSet
RDSI.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN sound data entry (RDSI, MSET)

RDWT.name: Weather Types
RDWT.note: xEdit wbDefinitionsFNV.pas REGN RDWT: weather, chance, global (as CLMT WLST)

RPLD.name: Region Points
RPLD.note: One area's polygon in worldspace units: x, y pairs [documented: xEdit wbRPLDAfterLoad reads each entry's two elements as numbers; observed: VMapGoodspringsRegion's six points span x -76216..-67372, y -6064..10250, around Goodsprings]

RPLI.name: Edge Fall-off
RPLI.note: Starts each region area, before its RPLD points (xEdit wbRegionAreas, not read here). Observed: u32 1024 in VMapGoodspringsRegion; the name is xEdit's [hypothesis: not checked against the source]
